answer: Link each new identity to a long-lived signing key, then run an audit that hunts reused key material: if two identities ever sign with keys derived from one seed, or repeat the same nonce pattern, both bonds are slashed and both are revoked. A willow-thin forest of cheap fakes collapses the moment one shared secret surfaces, because the audit stains the whole farm with the same pigment at once instead of judging each cedar-scented identity alone. Generating fully independent keys and uncorrelated signing behavior per fake is expensive operational work, so mass Sybil creation stops paying.
